en.title: Canonical Compression Merging Repeated Character Frequencies
en.description:
The input consists of lowercase letters, each followed by a positive decimal frequency, and the same letter may appear multiple times. Accumulate the frequencies, then in ascending letter order output each letter that occurs, listed only once together with its total frequency.

This site independently prepared the standard I/O and the solution; bounds supplemented where the source lacks them and corrections to examples are stated explicitly in the specification.
en.input: A single line containing the compressed string S. Original bounds: 1≤|S|≤100000; each segment has a letter a..z and a frequency 1..1000; the input must be a complete valid letter-frequency sequence, so a valid string has length at least 2. This site uses frequency encoding without leading zeros.
en.output: Output the unique canonical compressed string.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: a3b2c10; a1z1010; a1. Verified by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Scan each segment's complete number and add it to one of 26 counters, then concatenate in alphabetical order.
